title: Quantization contract oracle for JSON-RPC output stability under FP8/INT8
creator: Anika Shah
description: Background: After integrating FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles into our serving runtime, we observed intermittent violations of the JSON-RPC contract for structured outputs in low-latency paths. Objective: Build a contract oracle and automated harness that validates JSON-RPC responses (types, required fields, value coercions, and field ordering tolerances) across calibrated FP8/INT8 profiles during CI and nightly stability runs. The validator should be lightweight, deterministic when possible, and able to triage between quantization-induced numerical drift vs. tokenization/decoding variances.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic oracle that flags schema violations (missing/extra keys, wrong types) for JSON-RPC style responses across FP8/INT8 builds
Integration into CI such that any PR altering quantization profiles or runtime kernels triggers the oracle and fails on regression-level violations
A triage report that classifies violations into: structural (schema), semantic (enum/value set), and numerical fuzz (token segmentation/float rounding)
Nightly stability job producing historical trend charts and regression alerts for structured-output failures
test_plan: Create a corpus of 500 canonical JSON-RPC transactions derived from production prompts and synthetic edge cases (nested objects, optional fields, enum permutations)
Run baseline (float32) outputs to establish golden contracts and tolerated deviations for each transaction
Execute the harness across FP8 and INT8 calibrated model artifacts with N=3 seeds and compare results to baseline using the oracle rules
Record and dashboard violations; create auto-classified tickets for structural regressions
Gate any PR that increases structural regression rate beyond 0.1% on the canonical corpus
risk_mitigation: Keep the oracle conservative: structural checks are strict, numeric/semantic checks allow configurable tolerances
If false positives spike, fall back to a canary rollout policy that uses float32 for the first 5% of traffic while we investigate
Add quick-revert automation that switches routing to a verified-compatible model variant when burst regressions are detected
Coordinate with SDK/decoder owners on edge cases caused by tokenizer differences rather than quantization
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with runtime, inference QA, and SDK teams. Agreed canonical corpus scope.
2026-02-22: Prototype oracle implemented (Python) with structural checks and enum validators. Running locally against a 120-case subset.
2026-03-03: Integrated oracle into CI smoke stage; initial run flagged 7 structural mismatches on INT8 profile — root cause traced to truncated optional field in decoder loop.
2026-03-08: Decoder patch merged (PR #6148) and INT8 rerun reduced structural mismatches to 0 on the smoke subset. Planning expansion to 500-case corpus.
